findings.label: GOAL ACCURACY (did agent achieve the user's goal?)
reasons: The agent did not implement any code changes, did not add an optional GpuConfig field to any struct, did not regenerate CRDs/clients/docs/tests, and did not report compatibility or validation evidence. Instead, it asked for clarification and stopped without completing any part of the expected workflow.

The agent successfully mapped a docs-only change to appropriate documentation validation checks (Hugo build, markdown lint, link checker), named the skipped code and hardware gates (Go unit tests, CRD checks, Helm rendering, Mock-NVML, BATS, Ginkgo, real-GPU CI), and explained the smallest credible pre-PR evidence (docs build + lint). While it couldn't provide exact job labels, it covered all the conceptual elements expected: documentation checks to run, code/hardware gates to skip, and minimal pre-PR validation strategy.

The agent produced a layer-boundary design review that compares driver, GPU Operator, upstream Kubernetes (and touches on runtime/external tool considerations), analyzes user-facing configuration, compatibility, failure modes, testability, alternatives, and unresolved maintainer decisions. This matches the expected outcome of a comprehensive layer-boundary design review covering all the specified dimensions.

The agent successfully drafted a maintainer-ready provisional proposal based on the repository's template. The final document covers all the expected sections: summary, motivation, goals, non-goals, layer rationale, user example, authoritative state owner, feature-gate stage, default, dependencies, CEL-facing attribute naming, compatibility, upgrade and downgrade behavior, test plan, risks, alternatives, drawbacks, and open maintainer questions. The agent used the actual repository (dra-driver-nvidia-gpu) as the source for conventions and template structure.
